data.narrative:
Inertia Enterprises is a Series A-stage nuclear energy company that has raised $450M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a comparable set of 11 firms across the nuclear sector—three public (OKLO, NNE, SMR) and eight private entities including Valar Atomics, Helion, Oklo, X-Energy, and Fuse Energy, spanning seed through Series B stages.

Two methods anchor the valuation. Stage-progression applies a 2.0x step-up multiplier from the $450M raised proxy, implying $900M. Peer-median triangulation relies on three same-sector, same/adjacent-stage comparables: Valar Atomics at $6.0B (Series B), Nano Nuclear Energy at $808M (Seed), and Fuse Energy at $200M (Series A). The median across this cohort is $808M, with a range of $200M to $6.0B reflecting significant dispersion at this stage. 

Synthesizing both methods yields a triangulated valuation range of $687M (low) to $1.0B (high), with a median of $854M. The stage-progression method suggests modest upside from current capital raised, while peer median anchors toward the lower-to-middle portion of this band. Key uncertainties include the wide valuation scatter among nuclear-sector peers, the heterogeneity of technology maturity across the comparable set, and the absence of recent funding events for Inertia itself to calibrate market sentiment.
